signal: Paces raised an $11M Series A led by Navitas Capital to scale its clean-energy site-selection and development data platform

email.body1:
Will, saw Paces closed its $11M Series A led by Navitas to scale clean-energy development data.

Scaling that fast usually means more in-market developer accounts than the team can cover before they cool, and that is where pipeline leaks post-raise. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Paces off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Will, quick follow-up for Paces.

Post-Series-A, board expectations on pipeline jump faster than headcount can ramp, and most VPs cannot say precisely how many meetings the team needs to hit the new number. The gap shows up late, and the scramble costs a quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Paces needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Will, last bit of proof for Paces.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Paces' reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Will, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority right now, no problem at all. The fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-A motion? I will tailor it to Paces either way.
